decision: Classify as AMBIGUOUS_EFFECT / expected-behavior discovery, not a proven mis-click
facts: The probe changed the ボーカル counter from 0/20 to 1/20 and opened the vocal skill-entry panel.
The URL remained /produce and the allocation was uncommitted because 決定 was not pressed.
The calibration record observed the same panel-opening behavior for both tested stat columns and classifies it as normal behavior of allocating a point.
The initial probe used a visual estimate from a zoomed but uncalibrated clip, and the candidate causes included stale state, hitbox overlap, and inherent panel opening.
The calibration resolution reclassified the event as expected-behavior discovery and states that the click did not miss.
inferences: The panel opening is a documented side effect of allocation, so it cannot alone support a mis-click verdict.
A mis-click classification should follow repeated controlled observations that enumerate both expected and forbidden side effects, with fresh per-control grounding.
The correct current interpretation is bounded ambiguity/behavior discovery rather than a proven coordinate failure.
unknowns: The semantic identity of the skill-entry panel remains unknown.
The exact canvas hitbox and tolerance remain unknown.
A single probe does not establish whether all similar layouts behave identically outside the tested calibration samples.
reason: Both the expected counter increment and panel opening were observed, and repeated calibration identified panel opening as inherent behavior. More controlled evidence must precede any mis-click verdict; no action is permitted in this offline evaluation.
